issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court must independently decide the appeal by addressing the issues, grounds, evidence, and contentions requiring decision and giving reasons for its findings.
material_facts: The defendants appealed a preliminary decree in a partition suit, and the plaintiffs filed cross-objections.
The High Court modified the decree in a brief judgment without addressing the parties’ grounds, the cross-objections, the evidence, or the issues requiring decision.

The Supreme Court found that this deprived the appellants of their right to a proper first appeal and set aside the High Court’s judgment, remanding the appeal and cross-objections for fresh decision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the first appeal and cross-objections were remanded for decision afresh in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 96 read with Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a first appeal is a valuable right and, unless restricted by law, the case is open for rehearing on fact and law. The appellate judgment must state the points for determination, decisions, reasons, and any relief where the decree is reversed or varied, and must address the issues, evidence, and contentions pressed by the parties. The Court relied on Kurian Chacko v. Varkey Ouseph, AIR 1969 Kerala 316; Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari, (2001) 3 SCC 179; Madhukar v. Sangram, (2001) 4 SCC 756; H.K.N. Swami v. Irshad Basith, (2005) 10 SCC 243; Jagannath v. Arulappa, (2005) 12 SCC 303; B.V. Nagesh v. H.V. Sreenivasa Murthy, (2010) 13 SCC 530; State Bank of India v. Emmsons International Ltd., (2011) 12 SCC 174; and Vinod Kumar v. Gangadhar, 2014 (12) Scale 171.

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: A party pursued a first appeal from an original decree.
predicates.appellate_court_failed_to_address_materi: The appellate court did not address material issues, evidence, or contentions requiring decision.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an original decree is not decided after addressing the material issues, evidence, or contentions, the first appellate judgment is set aside and the case is remanded for a fresh decision.

issues.legal_issue: In a suit for partition and separate possession, the court must determine the character and source of the properties, how interests devolved, whether partition is feasible, and whether all properties and interested persons are included.
material_facts: The suit sought partition and separate possession of shares in family properties whose ownership and character were disputed.

The properties were said to include ancestral properties and properties claimed to have been bequeathed, but the High Court did not assess the evidence or determine the properties’ character, source of acquisition, or devolution before fixing shares.
The Supreme Court identified these matters as necessary to the proper disposal of the partition suit and directed the High Court to decide the appeal afresh on the merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was required to determine the nature and source of the properties, the devolution of interests, the feasibility of partition, and whether all properties and interested persons were before the court, on the evidence and applicable law.
issues.legal_principle: In a partition and separate-possession suit, the court must examine who originally owned each property and how it was acquired; whether it was self-acquired, ancestral, joint, or coparcenary property and who held interests in it; how an interest devolved on death, including the effect of intestate or testamentary succession; whether effective partition is possible and how it can be made; and whether all relevant properties and co-sharers, coparceners, co-owners, or joint owners are parties. These determinations must be based on the family relationships, evidence, and applicable law. The Court referred to Mulla, Hindu Law, 17th Edition, Chapter XVI, Partition and Reunion—Mitakshara Law, and directed consideration of the Hindu Succession Act and other related laws applicable to the issues.

predicates.partition_and_separate_possession_suit: A claimant sought partition of property and separate possession of a share against other interested persons.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks partition and separate possession, the court must determine the properties’ character and devolution, whether they can be partitioned, and whether all relevant properties and interested persons are included.

issues.legal_issue: A claimed concession does not excuse a first appellate court from deciding the merits when the record does not establish a written settlement or an intention to abandon the claim.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the High Court had decided the appeal on the appellants’ concession and therefore did not need to give detailed findings.

The appellants had made no written application to settle the dispute concerning any suit property, and the record did not show that they wished to abandon their claims or settle the matter concerning any properties.
The Supreme Court rejected the argument and held that the High Court should have examined the merits and determined the parties’ shares after considering the evidence and applicable law.
issues.conclusion: The alleged concession did not justify dispensing with a merits decision; the High Court was required to decide the parties’ claims on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: A first appellate court must determine the merits in accordance with its duties under Section 96 read with Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. An asserted concession does not remove that duty where there is no written settlement application and the record does not establish an intention to abandon claims or settle the dispute.

rule.if: first_appeal_from_original_decree and appeal_disposed_of_on_claimed_concession and written_settlement_application_absent and record_of_intent_to_abandon_or_settle_absent

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: A party pursued a first appeal from an original decree.
predicates.appeal_disposed_of_on_claimed_concession: The appellate court disposed of the appeal on the basis of an asserted concession by a party.
predicates.written_settlement_application_absent: No written application to settle the dispute was made.
predicates.record_of_intent_to_abandon_or_settle_ab: The record did not show that the party intended to abandon its claim or settle the dispute.

issues.definition: When a first appeal is disposed of on an asserted concession, but there is no written settlement application or record of an intention to abandon or settle, the appellate court must decide the merits.
